sources.reference: User-supplied reference photograph, 2026-10-07: a white Laser/ILCA on a launch trolley, used for the appearance and relative arrangement of blocks, ropes, control cleats and deck eyes. It is not a dimensioned survey. The simulator remains an ILCA 7; no sail, hull or rig physics dimensions are taken from the photograph.
sources.hardware: VISUAL ESTIMATE: all block, shackle, sheave, cleat, fairlead and deck-eye dimensions, tessellation, finish colours and placement offsets. Hardware roughness 0.84 and metalness 0 avoid hard reflections. Open-cheek proportions (0.70 height, 0.74 width, 0.275 chamfers), groove profiles (0.83/0.86 rim radii, 0.17/0.36 axial offsets), 1.6-times-tube fastener radii and 0.82-width bridges are modelling estimates. Rounded parts use 8 or 12 segments, tubes 6 and mounting pads 4 mm. Cleat jaws, fairlead offsets, eye pads and bow setback are visual proportions, not measured hardware. Hiking-strap estimates now live in hull-details.json alongside the reference-matched cockpit fittings. Class-sourced attachment positions already in data/laser.json stay unchanged. These are small low-poly visual fittings, not a branded or mechanically calibrated model.
sources.ropes: VISUAL ESTIMATE: rope radii, colours, six-sided sections, roughness 0.95, slack-loop sag, tail turns and radius. The floor coil uses 16 spans per turn and three rope radii of clearance. The mainsheet follows the existing traveller, boom blocks, ratchet and sheet hand. Its loaded span between boom blocks is straight; loopSag applies only to the loose hand-to-floor sheet tail and the outhaul tail's placement, not the loaded mainsheet. Added control-line routing is a visual approximation of the reference. No rope tension, friction, control purchase, sailing input or force changes. All data in this file is render-only.
